questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: A particle starts from rest and moves with constant acceleration. If it covers 45 m in the 5th second, what is its acceleration?

distractor_reasoning.A: Confuses distance in nth second formula with average velocity.
distractor_reasoning.C: Forgets the factor of 1/2 in the nth-second displacement formula.
distractor_reasoning.D: Divides the correct answer by 4 by mis-substituting n=5 as n².

questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: Two point charges +q and -q are separated by distance d. The electric field at the midpoint of the line joining them is directed:

options.A: Perpendicular to the line joining the charges

distractor_reasoning.C: Reverses the direction convention for field lines (which go from + to -).
distractor_reasoning.D: Incorrectly assumes fields from equal-magnitude opposite charges cancel at the midpoint.
distractor_reasoning.A: Confuses this dipole setup with the field along the perpendicular bisector of two like charges.

questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: The photoelectric effect demonstrates that light behaves as:

distractor_reasoning.A: This is exactly what the wave model predicts incorrectly (no threshold frequency) -- a common conceptual trap.
distractor_reasoning.C: Confuses this with disproven 19th-century aether theory, unrelated to photoelectric effect.
distractor_reasoning.D: Not a standard misconception but a plausible-sounding distractor for guessing students.

questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: A convex lens forms a real, inverted, diminished image. The object must be placed:

distractor_reasoning.D: At exactly 2F the image is same-size, not diminished -- a common off-by-one-case error.
distractor_reasoning.A: Object between focus and lens gives a virtual, magnified image, not real/diminished.
distractor_reasoning.B: At focus the image forms at infinity, not diminished.

questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: The moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its diameter is:

distractor_reasoning.B: This is the moment of inertia of a hollow (spherical shell), not solid, sphere.
distractor_reasoning.D: This is the moment of inertia of a solid disc/cylinder, a commonly confused formula.
distractor_reasoning.C: This is for a point mass or ring, not a solid sphere.

questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: True or False: If the velocity of an object is zero at an instant, its acceleration at that instant must also be zero.

answer_key.explanation: False -- e.g. a ball thrown up has zero velocity at the peak but non-zero (gravitational) acceleration.

questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: True or False: Electric field lines can intersect each other at a point where the field is zero.

answer_key.explanation: False -- field lines never intersect at all, since the field direction at any point must be unique.

questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: True or False: The speed of sound in air increases with an increase in humidity.

answer_key.explanation: True -- moist air has lower density than dry air (water vapour is lighter than N2/O2), so sound travels faster.

questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: True or False: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of incident light increases the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons.

answer_key.explanation: False -- intensity increases the number of photoelectrons emitted, not their maximum kinetic energy, which depends only on frequency.

questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: State Gauss's law and explain why it is useful for calculating the electric field of symmetric charge distributions.

rubric_points: States Gauss's law: total electric flux through a closed surface = enclosed charge / ε0
Notes the closed surface is a chosen 'Gaussian surface', not a physical object
Explains it simplifies field calculation when symmetry lets E be pulled out of the flux integral (spherical/cylindrical/planar symmetry)

questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: Explain the difference between an isothermal and an adiabatic process for an ideal gas.

rubric_points: Isothermal: temperature constant, requires heat exchange with surroundings
Adiabatic: no heat exchange (Q=0), temperature changes as work is done
Notes the adiabatic PV curve is steeper than the isothermal one (different exponent, gamma vs 1)

questions.subject: JEE Physics
questions.question_text: Explain why a figure skater spins faster when they pull their arms inward.

rubric_points: Identifies conservation of angular momentum (L = Iω) as no external torque acts
Explains pulling arms in reduces moment of inertia I
Concludes angular velocity ω must increase to keep L constant
